title: VS Code user settings and sync state
whyItMatters: The VS Code user folder holds personal settings, recent workspace names and the sign-in state for Settings Sync. Tokens pasted into settings and extension state can be reused by anyone with the disk.
source: VS Code docs, Settings file locations: user settings live in ~/.config/Code/User on Linux - https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/settings
notes: settings.json, keybindings.json, snippets and globalStorage/state.vscdb (Settings Sync state and extension storage) live here. The Flatpak and snap builds use different folders and are not matched. Contents are not read.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy settings.json and any snippet files you want to keep to a drive you are taking with you.
cleanup.signOut: Turn off Settings Sync in VS Code with the Settings Sync: Turn Off command, so the account stops trusting this machine.
steps: Open VS Code and turn Settings Sync off from the Accounts menu.
Uninstall Visual Studio Code with your package manager or software centre.
Delete the folder named in the plan using the file manager.
cleanup.risk: Removes personal VS Code settings, keybindings, snippets and sign-in state from this machine. Settings already synced stay in the account.
